tagline.text: A little Amsterdam in celosia colors, blooming on a Cebu ridgeline

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,500 per person (half day from Cebu City)

children.text: A terraced flower garden on the slopes of Sirao, a mountain village behind Cebu City, layered with red and yellow celosia in full bloom. Windmills and Dutch-style ornaments have earned it the nickname "little Amsterdam," and it pairs well with the Temple of Leah and Tops Lookout for a half-day drive through the highlands.
Sirao Flower Garden sits in the mountain village of Sirao, north of Cebu City. From the Cebu IT Park and Lahug area, it's about
up the Transcentral Highway into the mountains, roughly
40 minutes to 1 hour
by car. At an elevation of several hundred meters, the air here is cooler than the coastal downtown, and green ridges and valleys layer into the distance beyond the garden.
This garden wasn't originally a tourist attraction. It began when a caretaker on the farm of landowner Elena Sy Chua, a former flight attendant, planted celosia to sell for All Saints' Day (
November 1
); when photos of the red-and-yellow flower field spread on social media, crowds started flocking in. It officially opened around the Santo Niño feast in
January 2016

, and inspired by Dutch tulip gardens, the owners put up windmills and adopted the nickname "little Amsterdam." Because celosia shares the red and yellow of the Santo Niño's vestments, Cebuanos also call it the "Santo Niño flower."

Sirao today is home to several similar flower gardens clustered together, including the original Sirao Garden (Little Amsterdam) and the neighboring Sirao Pictorial Garden. Besides celosia, sunflowers, marigolds, cosmos, chrysanthemums, and dahlias are planted in rotation by season, alongside windmills, heart-shaped structures, a giant hand sculpture, Dutch-house murals, and vintage cars as photo props scattered throughout. The garden has also been used as a filming location for Filipino dramas and movies.

Don't expect grand natural scenery — think of it instead as a place to take photos among colorful flowers and props while enjoying the cool mountain breeze, and you'll come away satisfied. It suits couples, families, and travelers with parents in tow based in Cebu City, and the most popular route pairs it with the Temple of Leah and Tops Lookout, also in the highlands, for a half-day loop.

Red, yellow, and pink celosia planted in terraces down the slope are the garden's centerpiece. A path winding through the flower beds lets you frame the blooms together with the mountain ridgeline. Flower conditions vary by planting schedule, so check recent visitor photos before you go.

The windmill that inspired the "little Amsterdam" nickname is Sirao's signature photo spot. The windmill at the original garden also doubles as a gift shop and lookout — climb to the top for a view over the whole flower field.

Flower-decorated heart arches and benches, a giant hand sculpture you can pose on as if standing in a giant's palm, and Dutch-house murals are scattered around as photo props. Lines form at the most popular spots on weekends.
The original Sirao Garden focuses simply on the flower fields, while the neighboring Sirao Pictorial Garden has more sculptures and photo zones. Entry runs about
each, so many travelers with time to spare visit both.

Being higher up than downtown Cebu, it's a pleasant spot to relax in a hammock or on a shaded bench. Buy a drink or snack at the garden's café or stall and take in the valley view at a leisurely pace.

blocks.title: Pairing with the Temple of Leah and Tops Lookout

children.text: Along the same Transcentral Highway are the Temple of Leah, styled after a Roman temple, and Tops Lookout, with a sweeping view over downtown Cebu and Mactan. Chartering a habal-habal or vehicle to cover all three in one trip is the most efficient route.

blocks.title: Sunset Dinner in the Busay Highlands

children.text: Leave the garden in the late afternoon and have dinner at one of the view restaurants in the Busay area to look down over the lights of downtown Cebu and Mactan. It's especially beautiful around sunset.
Depart your Cebu City accommodation; catch a habal-habal or chartered vehicle in front of JY Square Mall
Arrive at Sirao Flower Garden, photograph the flower fields and windmill in the soft morning light
Explore the neighboring garden or take a break at a café
Tour the Temple of Leah
Lunch at a view restaurant in the Busay area
Enjoy views of downtown Cebu and Mactan from Tops Lookout, then return to the city

If you set out later in the afternoon, it also works to reverse the order — visit the Temple of Leah first, enjoy the afternoon light at Sirao Garden, and finish with sunset and the night view at Tops Lookout.
Direct flights from Incheon or Busan in Korea to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) take about
4 hours 30 minutes to 5 hours
, and about
1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila.
From the airport to Sirao is about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
, passing through downtown Cebu City. Most travelers check into their Cebu City or Mactan accommodation first and set aside a separate day for this trip.
In front of JY Square Mall in Lahug is where habal-habal drivers gather for Busay and Sirao. A one-way trip to Sirao costs about
per person and takes about
30–45 minutes
Since it's hard to find a ride back, it's more convenient to negotiate a round-trip charter (about
per person, including waiting time) covering Sirao Garden, the Temple of Leah, and Tops Lookout. Agree clearly on the stops and waiting time before you set off.
Since
March 2026
the Cebu BRT has partly operated the SRP–IT Park section, so you can also ride the BRT from the southern downtown to IT Park, then take a habal-habal at JY Square Mall, about
10–15 minutes
away on foot. BRT fares and free-ride periods may change, so check the latest notices.
A one-way Grab or taxi ride from central Cebu City costs about
. It's hard to catch a ride back up in the mountains, so it's best to pay the driver a waiting fee and ask them to wait for the round trip.
If you're traveling with family or a group, chartering a vehicle with driver for a half day (about
) to cover the Temple of Leah and Tops Lookout together is by far the most convenient option.

The Transcentral Highway is steep and winding. Visibility worsens in rain or afternoon fog, so only drive yourself if you're comfortable with mountain roads. Some garden parking lots charge a small fee.
Sirao is open year-round, and because flowers are planted in rotating sections, you'll find some blooms whatever month you visit. Weather-wise, though, the
December–May
dry season is best.
January to March
in particular brings clear skies and pleasant highland temperatures around
. In
April and May
, strong midday sun can make the shade-poor flower fields feel hot, so an early morning visit is better.
During the
June–November
rainy season, clouds and rain roll in most afternoons, and fog sometimes settles on the mountain road. After heavy rain, flowers can be damaged and dirt paths turn muddy. Around
October
, ahead of All Saints' Day, and in
January
, during Sinulog festival, celosia tends to bloom abundantly — but visitor numbers rise along with it. For photography, aim for the soft light of
7–9 AM

Lodging near Sirao is scarce, so it's typical to stay in Cebu City and visit for half a day. The Lahug/IT Park area is close to the garden and has plenty of restaurants, with business hotels from about
a night up to high-end hotels above
. To soak in more mountain air, there are also small lodge-style stays and campsites in the Busay highlands.

Inside the garden, a café and stall sell drinks and simple snacks, but the food options are limited. The Busay highlands have several view restaurants serving Filipino food while overlooking downtown Cebu's night skyline, with the long-running Lantaw Busay branch a favorite. If you're in Cebu, be sure to try the whole roast pig lechon, and sutukil grills paired with puso (rice steamed in woven coconut-leaf pouches). Night-market-style food courts like IT Park's Sugbo Mercado are also popular for dinner.
If photography is your priority, go early in the morning. The light is softer and there are fewer people, so you won't have to queue at the photo spots.
Flower conditions vary considerably by season and planting schedule. Checking recent photo reviews on social media or map apps just before your visit can help avoid disappointment.
It's cooler and breezier up the mountain than downtown, but the sun is strong. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and a light jacket.
Transport back is the biggest challenge. Whether by habal-habal or taxi, negotiate a round-trip rate with waiting time included beforehand.
Pay entrance and transport fees in cash. There's no ATM up the mountain, so prepare small bills in the city.
Don't step into the flower beds for photos — use only the designated paths and photo zones. Trampling or picking flowers can result in a fine or being asked to leave.
When pairing with the Temple of Leah and Tops Lookout, visiting Sirao in the morning and Tops around sunset lets you see both the flowers and the night view in the best light.
The two gardens have different owners, so their hours differ too. The Original Sirao Garden is open
8 AM–5 PM
on Mondays,
8 AM–6 PM
Tuesday to Friday, and
7 AM–6 PM
on weekends, while Sirao Pictorial Garden is open daily
6 AM–6:30 PM
. If you arrive early in the morning, look around the Pictorial Garden first.
The Transcentral Highway is a mountain road with steep grades and sharp curves. Always wear a helmet on a habal-habal, and ask the driver to slow down in rain or heavy fog.
After rain, the garden's dirt paths and steps get slippery. Avoid high heels and wear sneakers instead.
Bees and insects are common around the flower beds. If you're allergic to bee stings, bring medication, and avoid strong perfume.
On weekend and holiday afternoons, traffic backs up on the narrow mountain road and parking space runs short.
Habal-habal fares vary by driver, so confirm the price before boarding, and don't agree to extra charges demanded after arrival.
During the rainy season and typhoon season, landslides or falling rocks can close the road, so check the weather before you set out.
